Definition: An identifier data field which describes the user-defined name for the sample.
Guidance: The sample ID should represent the identifier assigned to the sample at time of collection, for which all the descriptive information applies. Every sample ID from a single submitter must be unique. The ID may use any format, but should be concise, consistent within the lab, and informative where possible. If the original sample ID is unknown or cannot be provided, leave blank or provide a null value.

Definition: A data field which describes the identifier used to specify an epidemiologically detected case of disease.
Guidance: Provide the case identifer. The case ID greatly facilitates linkage between laboratory and epidemiological data. The case ID may be considered identifiable information. Consult the data steward before sharing.

Definition: An identifier field which describes the International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC) umbrella accession number of the BioProject to which the BioSample belongs.
Guidance: Required if submission is linked to an umbrella BioProject. An umbrella BioProject links together related BioProjects. A valid BioProject umbrella accession has prefix PRJN, PRJE or PRJD. Your laboratory can have one or many BioProjects.

Definition: An identifier field which describes the International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC) accession number of the BioProject(s) to which the BioSample belongs.
Guidance: Required if submission is linked to a BioProject. BioProjects are an organizing tool that links together raw sequence data, assemblies, and their associated metadata. A valid BioProject accession has prefix PRJN, PRJE or PRJD and is created once at the beginning of a new sequencing project. Your laboratory can have one or many BioProjects.

Definition: An identifier field which describes the identifier assigned to a BioSample in International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC) archives.
Guidance: Store the accession returned from the BioSample submission. NCBI BioSamples will have the prefix SAMN.

Definition: An identifier field which describes the Sequence Read Archive (SRA), European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) or DDBJ Sequence Read Archive (DRA) identifier linking raw read data, methodological metadata and quality control metrics submitted to the International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC).
Guidance: Store the accession assigned to the submitted "run". NCBI-SRA accessions start with SRR.

Definition: A unique identifier that denotes an assembly record submitted to the International Nucleotide Sequence Database Collaboration (INSDC).
Guidance: Store the versioned accession assigned to the submitted sequence e.g. the GenBank accession version.

Definition: Identifier for the physical specimen.
Guidance: Include a URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) in the form of a URL providing a direct link to the physical host specimen. If the specimen was destroyed in the process of analysis, electronic images (e-vouchers) are an adequate substitute for a physical host voucher specimen. If a URI is not available, a museum-provided globally unique identifier (GUID) can be used. If no persistent unique identifier is available, follow the INSDC guidance for populating the voucher_specimen attribute using standard triplets for institution codes (i.e., /specimen_voucher=.[<institution-code>:[<collection-code>:]]<specimen_id>.): http://www.insdc.org/controlled-vocabulary-specimenvoucher-qualifier
Example(s): URI example: http://portal.vertnet.org/o/fmnh/mammals?id=33e55cfe-330b-40d9-aaae-8d042cba7542, INSDC triplet example: UAM:Mamm:52179

Definition: The person (or organization) responsible for a specific data set.
Guidance: The official organization name should be used (avoid abbreviations, alternate names as much as possible).
Example(s): National Malaria Control Program, Ghana Health Service

Definition: The name of the agency that collected the original sample.
Guidance: The name of the agency should be written out in full, (with minor exceptions) and be consistent across multiple submissions.
Example(s): Centre for Infectious Disease Research in Zambia

Definition: A data field which describes the name or job title of the contact responsible for follow-up regarding the sample.
Guidance: Provide the name of an individual or their job title. As personnel turnover may render the contact's name obsolete, it is more preferable to provide a job title for ensuring accuracy of information and institutional memory. If the information is unknown or cannot be provided, leave blank or provide a null value.

Definition: The email address of the contact responsible for follow-up regarding the sample.
Guidance: The email address can represent a specific individual or laboratory.

Definition: The mailing address of the agency submitting the sample.
Guidance: The mailing address should be in the format: Street number and name, City, State/Province/Region, Country, Postal Code/Zip Code
Example(s): CIDRZ Central Laboratory, Kalingalinga Health Centre, Corner of Alick Nkhata and Condor Roads, Kalingalinga, Lusaka, Zambia.

Definition: The reason that the sample was collected.
Guidance: Select a value from the pick list in the template.

Definition: Further details pertaining to the reason the sample was collected.
Guidance: Provide a free text description of the sampling strategy or samples collected.
Example(s): To evaluate the effectiveness of HPPD inhibitors from the β-triketone class of herbicides against both susceptible and pyrethroid-resistant strains of key mosquito vectors responsible for transmitting malaria, dengue, Zika, and other emerging viral diseases. [DOI: 10.1186/s13071-025-06939-0]

Definition: A sequence of characters used to identify, name, or characterize the study.
An official descriptive name of a document, e.g. the long name of a study protocol provided by the study sponsor.
Example(s): Anopheles albimanus strain:STELCA principal haplotype Genome sequencing and assembly

Definition: An uncontrolled observational study containing a detailed report of the diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of an individual patient. Case reports also contain some demographic information about the patient (for example, age, gender, ethnic origin).
Guidance: Provide the study descriptor if the sample was collected as part of a study. Pick a value from the pick list provided.

Definition: The date on which a study began.
Guidance: Provide the study start date in ISO 8601 format, i.e. "YYYY-MM-DD".

Definition: The date on which a study completes.
Guidance: Provide the study completing date in ISO 8601 format, i.e. "YYYY-MM-DD".

Definition: A sequence-of characters used to identify, name, or characterize the study site.
Guidance: It is a unique identifier for the geographic or institutional location where a study is conducted, e.g., a hospital, clinic, or village where participants are enrolled and the study is implemented.

Definition: A population is a collection of individuals from the same taxonomic class living, counted or sampled at a particular site or in a particular area.
Guidance: Record the sample collection targeted population group accuratly in the template. Pick a value from the pick list provided.

Definition: The specific sex, either male, female, or mixed of the subject group being studied.
Guidance: Pick a value from the pick list provided.

Definition: An infectious disease control strategy that has a vector control action specification as part.
Guidance: Select a value(s) from the pick-up list.
Example(s): Indoor residual spraying vector control strategy [APOLLO:SV_00000391],  surface drainage [IDOMAL:0000680], Lido system [IDOMAL:0000679]

Definition: Strictly, a substance intended to kill members of the class Insecta. In common usage, any substance used for preventing, destroying, repelling or controlling insects.
Guidance: Use standard classes. Select a value from the pick list provided.

Definition: The country of origin of the sample.
Guidance: Provide the country name from the pick list in the template

Definition: A primary administrative division of a country, such as a state in the United States
Guidance: Provide the name of the primary administrative subdivision (such as a province, state or territory) of the country where the sample originated, using official name from the GAZ (Gazetteer) geography ontology. Search for geography terms here: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/gaz

Definition: A subdivision of a second-order administrative division
Guidance: Provide the name of the second-order administrative subdivision (such as a district) of the country where the sample originated, using official name from the GAZ (Gazetteer) geography ontology. Search for geography terms here: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/gaz

Definition: A subdivision of a third-order administrative division
Guidance: Provide the name of the third-order administrative subdivision of a country, using official name from the GAZ (Gazetteer) geography ontology.
Example(s): City of Cape Town Metropolitan Municipality

Definition: A subdivision of a fourth-order administrative division
Guidance: Provide the name of the fourth-order administrative subdivision of a country, using official name from the GAZ (Gazetteer) geography ontology. Search for geography terms here: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/gaz

Definition: The user-defined identifier assigned to the environmental location from which a specimen or sample is taken.
Guidance: Store the identifier for the site from which a sample was taken. The "site" is user defined .This could be a household, a river bank (for vector sampling), a health facility room, or any other location. Please use the same site ID for all samples from a given site, regardless of when these samples were taken. Any important changes in site location, should be represented with a new site ID. For privacy reasons, consult a data steward before sharing, or ensure the sampling site ID is coded, anonymized, or otherwise protected.

Definition: The latitude coordinates of the geographical location of sample collection.
Guidance: Provide latitude coordinates if available and if ethicly acceptable to share. Specify as degrees latitude in format "d[d.dddd] N|S".

Definition: The longitude coordinates of the geographical location of sample collection.
Guidance: Provide longitude coordinates if available and if ethicly acceptable to share. Specify as degrees longitude in format "d[dd.dddd] W|E".

Definition: Height above sea level or above the earth's surface.
Guidance: The altitude of the sample is the vertical distance between Earth's surface above Sea Level and the sampled position in the air. Provide the numeric value of the altitude and the abreviated unit.

Definition: The vertical distance below local surface. For sediment or soil samples depth is measured from sediment or soil surface, respectively. Depth can be reported as an interval for subsurface samples MIXS:0000018.
Guidance: Provide the numeric value of the altitude and the abreviated unit.

Definition: The type of material from which the specimen was obtained. Specimens are usually categorized as food, body products or tissues, or environmental material.
Guidance: Select a value from the pick list provided in the template.

Definition: Describes the physical, environmental, and/or local geographical source of the biological sample from which the sample was derived.
Guidance: Provide a descriptor of an environmental site. Use the pick list provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the pick list, use this look-up service to identify a standardized term: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/envo. If not applicable, leave blank.

Definition: An environmental system which can sustain and allow the growth of an Anopheles mosquito population.
Guidance: Provid a free text description of the breeding habita, such as Animal drinking point, Berkat, Birkas, Borehole, Broken bucket, Car tyre, Cement block, Cistern, Construction water storage reservoir, Construction water tank, Dam, Discarded tyre, Discarded vehicle part, Ditch, Drain, Fish pond, Flower pot, Garbage can, Pond, Pool, Puddle, Rain catchment, Stagnant rain water, Tyre, Uncovered ground septic tank, Well.

Definition: Type of the breeding site.
Guidance: Provide the type of the breeding site from the pick list.

Definition: Shortest straight‑line (Euclidean) distance from the centre of the household to the nearest identified breeding habitat.
Guidance: Provide the shortest straight-line distance from the centre of the household to the nearest identified breeding habitat, in metres (m).

Definition: The number of mosquitoes present in a defined area or environment at a given time.
Guidance:
Estimating mosquito density is vital for understanding vector population dynamics and assessing the risk of malaria transmission. This estimation helps guide vector control interventions and monitor their effectiveness. 
Example: If a CDC light trap placed outside a house collects 50 mosquitoes during one night, the mosquito density can be expressed as 50 mosquitoes per trap per night. 
In another scenario, a larval survey in a breeding site may reveal an average of 30 larvae per dip sample, indicating the larval mosquito density in that habitat.

Definition: The percentage of female anopheline mosquitoes of a prarticular species that bear sporozoites in their salivary glands.
The number of bites per person in a certain period of time.
Guidance: Record the man biting rate in the following format: X bites/person/unit time. Example: 60 bites/person/night.

Definition: The date on which the sample was collected.
Guidance: Record the collection date accurately in the template. Required granularity includes year, month and day. Before sharing this data, ensure this date is not considered identifiable information. If this date is considered identifiable, it is acceptable to add "jitter" to the collection date by adding or subtracting calendar days. Do not change the collection date in your original records. Alternatively, ”received date” may be used as a substitute in the data you share. The date should be provided in ISO 8601 standard format "YYYY-MM-DD".

Definition: The precision to which the "sample collection date" was provided.
Guidance: Provide the precision of granularity to the ""day"", ""month"", or ""year"" for the date provided in the ""sample collection date"" field. The ""sample collection date"" will be truncated to the precision specified upon export; ""day"" for ""YYYY-MM-DD"","&" ""month"" for ""YYYY-MM"", or ""year"" for ""YYYY"".

Definition: The date on which the sample was collected, or sampling began for a continuous sample.
Guidance: If your sample is a continuous sample please use this field to capture your start date. Sample collection date is critical for surveillance and many types of analyses. Required granularity includes year, month and day. The date should be provided in ISO 8601 standard format "YYYY-MM-DD".

Definition: The time at which sample collection began.
Guidance: Provide the sample collection start time, if sampling occurs during a certain period of time that is important for downstream analysis. Provide this time in ISO 8601 24hr format, in your local time.

Definition: The date on which sample collection ended for a continuous sample.
Guidance: Provide the date that sample collection ended in ISO 8601 format i.e. YYYY-MM-DD

Definition: The time at which sample collection ended.
Guidance: Provide this time in ISO 8601 24hr format, in your local time.

Definition: The descriptive time of day during which the sample was collected.
Guidance: If known, select a value from the pick list. The time of sample processing matters especially for grab samples, as fecal concentration in wastewater fluctuates over the course of the day.

Definition: The amount of time over which the sample was collected.
Guidance: Provide the numerical value of time.

Definition: The units of the time duration measurement of sample collection.
Guidance: Provide the unit from the pick list.

Definition: The date on which the sample was received.
Guidance: The date the sample was received by a lab that was not the point of collection. ISO 8601 standard "YYYY-MM-DD".

Definition: The title of the sample or specimen
Guidance:
A specimen (or sample) title should be short and informative. Each specimen title must be unique in a submission. E.g. 1) Escherichia coli O104:H4 str. C227-11 clinical isolate 2010_333_NC-6 
2) CD8+ T cells from female TSG6-knockout BALB/c mouse 
3) Human metagenome isolated from urine of healthy female.

Definition: A data field which describes the name of the source collection and unique culture identifier.
Guidance: Example Guidance: Format: .<institution-code>:[<collection-code>:]<culture_id>. For more information, see http://www.insdc.org/controlled-vocabulary-culturecollection-qualifier.

Definition: A substance obtained from an anatomical part of an organism e.g. tissue, blood.
Guidance: Provide a descriptor if an anatomical material was sampled. Use the pick list provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the pick list, use this look-up service to identify a standardized term: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/uberon. If not applicable, leave blank.

Definition: An anatomical part of an organism e.g. oropharynx.
Guidance: Provide a descriptor if an anatomical part was sampled. Use the pick list provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the pick list, use this look-up service to identify a standardized term: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/uberon. If not applicable, leave blank.

Definition: A substance excreted/secreted from an organism e.g. feces, urine, sweat.
Guidance: Provide a descriptor if a body product was sampled. Use the pick list provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the pick list, use this look-up service to identify a standardized term: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/uberon. If not applicable, leave blank.

Definition: A data field which describes the substance obtained from the natural or man-made environment.
Guidance: Provide a descriptor if an environmental material was sampled. Use the pick list provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the pick list, use this look-up service to identify a standardized term: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/envo. If not applicable, leave blank.

Definition: The process used to collect the sample e.g. phlebotomy, necropsy.
Guidance: Provide a descriptor if a collection method was used for sampling. Use the pick list provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the pick list, use this look-up service to identify a standardized term: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/obi. If not applicable, leave blank.

Definition: The name and version of a particular protocol used for sampling.
Guidance: Provide the name and version of the protocol used to collect the samples.
Example(s): Standard Operating Procedure for the assembly and deployment of ovitraps.’ protocols. Io https://www.protocols.io/view/standard-operating-procedure-for-assembly-and-depl-cbgpsjvn

Definition: The instrument or container used to collect the sample e.g. swab.
Guidance: Provide a descriptor if a collection device was used for sampling. Use the pick list provided in the template. If a desired term is missing from the pick list, use this look-up service to identify a standardized term: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/obi. If not applicable, leave blank.

Definition: A laboratory providing analyses of samples collected in clinical care or research.
Guidance: The laboratory that actually performed the test and that is also therefore the source of the data.
Example(s): Centre Pasteur du Cameroun – Central Reference Laboratory

Definition: Indicates the person or authoritative body who made an identification. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/ncit/classes/http%253A%252F%252Fpurl.obolibrary.org%252Fobo%252FNCIT_C164229
Example(s): Centre Pasteur du Cameroun – Central Reference Laboratory

Definition: Any processing applied to the sample during or after receiving the sample.
Guidance: Critical for interpreting data. Select all the applicable processes from the pick list. If parasite was passaged, include information in "lab host", "passage number", and "passage method" fields. If none of the processes in the pick list apply, put "not applicable".

Definition: Name and description of the laboratory host used to propagate the source organism or material from which the sample was obtained.
Guidance: Type of cell line used for propagation. Select a value form the pick list. If not passaged, put "not applicable".

Definition: Number of passages.
Guidance: Provide number of known passages. If not passaged, put "not applicable"

Definition: Description of how organism was passaged.
Guidance: Free text. Provide a short description. If not passaged, put "not applicable".
Example(s): Culture of Plasmodium falciparum blood stages v1.0, WWARN Procedure, 2023. https://www.iddo.org/sites/default/files/publication/2023-09/inv01-culture-of-plasmodium-falciparum-blood-stages.pdf

Definition: Detailed information regarding the processing applied to a sample during or after receiving the sample.
Guidance: Provide a free text description of any processing details applied to a sample.
Example(s): Parasitemia was adjusted to 1-5% by mixing infected erythrocytes with uninfected erythrocytes (blood group O).

Definition: The type of role that the sample represents in the experiment.
Guidance: Samples can play different types of roles in experiments. A sample under study in one experiment may act as a control or be a replicate of another sample in another experiment. This field is used to distinguish samples under study from controls, replicates, etc.  If the sample acted as an experimental control or a replicate, select a role type from the picklist. If the sample was not a control, leave blank or select ""Not Applicable"".

Definition: The details regarding the experimental control contained in the sample.
Guidance: Provide details regarding the nature of the reference strain used as a control, or what is was used to monitor.
Example(s): A well-characterized laboratory clone or reference strain 3D7 clone was used as positive control to standardize assays and compare parasite growth or drug susceptibility.

Definition: A procedure used for the detection of the pathogen causing the disease.
Guidance: Select all procedures used for parasite detection from the pick list provided in the template.

Definition: The biomaterial extracted from samples for the purpose of sequencing.
Guidance: Provide the biomaterial extracted from the pick list in the template.

Definition: A description of how any data elements were altered to preserve patient privacy.
Guidance: If applicable, provide a description of how each data element was abstracted.
Example(s): Jitter added to publicly shared collection dates to prevent re-identifiability.

Definition: The act, process and logistical considerations of the physical or environmental conditions under which the biological sample is maintained.
The date that a biospecimen was processed.
Guidance: Provide the sample processed date in ISO 8601 format, i.e. "YYYY-MM-DD". The sample may be collected and processed (e.g. filtered, extraction) on the same day, or on different dates.

Definition: The name of the agency, organization or institution with which the individual who performed the isolation procedure is affiliated.
Guidance: Provide the name of the agency, organization or institution that isolated the original isolate in full (avoid abbreviations). If the information is unknown or cannot be provided, leave blank or provide a null value.

Definition: The specific laboratory affiliation of the individual who performed the isolation procedure.
Guidance: Provide the name of the specific laboratory that that isolated the original isolate (avoid abbreviations). If the information is unknown or cannot be provided, leave blank or provide a null value.

Definition: The name or title of the contact responsible for follow-up regarding the isolate.
Guidance: Provide the name of an individual or their job title. As personnel turnover may render the contact's name obsolete, it is prefereable to provide a job title for ensuring accuracy of information and institutional memory. If the information is unknown or cannot be provided, leave blank or provide a null value.

Definition: The email address of the contact responsible for follow-up regarding the isolate.
Guidance: Provide the email associated with the listed contact. As personnel turnover may render an individual's email obsolete, it is more prefereable to provide an address for a position or lab, to ensure accuracy of information and institutional memory. If the information is unknown or cannot be provided, leave blank or provide a null value.

Definition: The date on which the isolate was isolated from a sample.
Guidance: Provide the date according to the ISO 8601 standard "YYYY-MM-DD", "YYYY-MM" or "YYYY".

Definition: The date on which the isolate was received by the laboratory.
Guidance: Provide the date according to the ISO 8601 standard "YYYY-MM-DD", "YYYY-MM" or "YYYY".

Definition: The user-defined identifier for the isolate, as provided by the laboratory that originally isolated the isolate.
Guidance: Provide the isolate_ID created by the lab that first isolated the isolate (i.e. the original isolate ID). If the information is unknown or cannot be provided, leave blank or provide a null value. If only an alternate isolate ID is known (e.g. the ID from your lab, if your lab did not isolate the isolate from the original sample), make sure to include it in the alternative_isolate_ID field.

Definition: An alternative isolate_ID assigned to the isolate by another organization.
Guidance: Alternative isolate IDs should be provided in the in a prescribed format which consists of the ID followed by square brackets (no space in between the ID and bracket) containing the short form of ID provider’s agency name i.e. ID[short organization code]. An example of a properly formatted alternative_isolate_identifier would be e.g. XYZ4567[CFIA]. Multiple alternative isolate IDs can be provided, separated by semi-colons.

Definition: The identifier assigned to a progenitor isolate derived from an isolate that was directly obtained from a sample.
Guidance: If your sequence data pertains to progeny of an original isolate, provide the progeny_isolate_ID.

Definition: Taxonomic name of the organism.
Guidance: Select the "Plasmodium" species from the picklist . If another Plasmodium species is being sequenced, provide the taxonomic name from NCBITaxon. Search for taxonomy terms at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols/ontologies/ncbitaxon.

Definition: A parasite that is bred to have some uniform behavioral, morphological, physiological, or genetic characteristics with similarly bred parasite organisms. A strain of a species. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/ncbitaxon/classes/http%253A%252F%252Fpurl.obolibrary.org%252Fobo%252FNCBITaxon_strain
Guidance: If the isolate represents or is derived from, a lab reference strain or strain from a type culture collection, provide the strain identifier.

Definition: A further sub-classification of the organism strain.

A genetic characteristics information that is about the genetic material of an organism and minimally includes information about the genetic background and can in addition contain information about specific alleles, genetic modifications, etc.
Guidance: Genotype information can be: Mus musculus wild type (in this case the genetic population background information is Mus musculus), C57BL/6J Hnf1a+/- (in this case, C57BL/6J is the genetic population background information and Hnf1a+/- is the allele information

Definition: The assemblage of traits or outward appearance of an individual. It is the product of interactions between genes and the environment.
Guidance: The observable characteristics in an individual resulting from the expression of genes; the clinical presentation of an individual with a particular genotype.

Definition: Any method designed to identify the species of the insect specimen under study, usually caught /isolated from a field population.
NCBI Taxon id of the second host (mosquito vector), e.g., taxid:7157
A unique identifier by which each second host (mosquito vector) can be referred to e.g. #131
Guidance: Should be a unique, user-defined identifier. This ID can help link laboratory data with epidemiological data, however, is likely sensitive information. Consult the data steward.

Definition: The commonly used name of the second host.
Guidance: Common name or scientific name are required if there was a second host. Common name examples e.g. human, bat. Select a value from the pick list. If the sample was environmental, put "not applicable".

Definition: The taxonomic, or scientific name of the second host.
Guidance: Common name or scientific name are required if there was a second host. Scientific name should include the genus and species names of the host, e.g. Homo sapiens. Select a value from the pick list. If the sample was environmental, put "not applicable".

Definition: Vector species complex
Guidance: Group of closely related species that are morphologically similar in all main life stages (egg, larva, pupa, and adult) but moleculary different. E.g., Anopheles gambiae complex.

Definition: Group of closely related species, that are different in one or more life stages and molecular different. E.g., Anopheles funestus group.
Name of sub_species of organism from which sample was obtained. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/iceo/classes/http%253A%252F%252Fpurl.obolibrary.org%252Fobo%252FNCBITaxon_subspecies
A strain of a species. https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/ncbitaxon/classes/http%253A%252F%252Fpurl.obolibrary.org%252Fobo%252FNCBITaxon_strain
Guidance: If the isolate represents or is derived from, a lab reference strain or strain from a type culture collection, provide the strain identifier.

Definition: A genetic characteristics information that is about the genetic material of an organism and minimally includes information about the genetic background and can in addition contain information about specific alleles, genetic modifications, etc.
Guidance: Genotype information can be: Mus musculus wild type (in this case the genetic population background information is Mus musculus), C57BL/6J Hnf1a+/- (in this case, C57BL/6J is the genetic population background information and Hnf1a+/- is the allele information

Definition: A heritable change in the sensitivity of a pest population that is reflected in the repeated failure of a product to achieve the expected level of control when used according to the label recommendation for that pest species.
Guidance: The observable characteristics in an individual resulting from the expression of genes; the clinical presentation of an individual with a particular genotype.

Definition: The developmental stages of mosquitoes belonging to the genus Anopheles.
A subject sex is the phenotypic sex of given subject (human or animal) related to a given investigation, study, and/or specimen.
Guidance: If known, select a value from the pick list.

Definition: A quality which refers to vectors.
Guidance: An attribute of a vector is any measurable or descriptive property of that mosquito that affects transmission, biology, or ecology.

Definition: Describes the health (or disease) status of the second host at the time of sample collection.
Guidance: Report the physiological condition, other infection status, nutritional status, age (grade), or fitness condition of the mosquito vector. Select one or multiple values, from the pick list.
Example(s): Presence of filarial worms; Nutritional status: Sugar content (energy reserve): High

Definition: This variable indicates whether the mosquitoes collected are considered invasive or native.
Guidance: Note: An invasive species  is a non-native species that establishes in a new ecosystem, and causes, or has the potential to cause, harm to the environment, economy, or human health.

Definition: The numerical value of the human population inhabiting a defined sampling area that contributes to parasite transmission.
Guidance: Where known, provide the numerical value of population size, i.e. the number of people.

Definition: The range of the human population inhabiting a defined sampling area that contributes to parasite transmission.
Guidance: Where the sampling area human population is not well known, provide an estimation of population size by selecting a value from the picklist.

Definition: The numerical value describing the number of humans per geographical area in a sampling area.
Guidance: Provide the numerical value of the population density in the sampling area.

Definition: The unit describing the number of humans per geographical area in a sampling area.
Guidance: Provide the unit of the population density in the sampling area.

Definition: An accumulation of water of varying size.
Guidance: The term body of water most often refers to large accumulations of water, such as oceans, seas, and lakes, but it includes smaller pools of water such as ponds, wetlands, or more rarely, puddles. A body of water does not have to be still or contained; Rivers, streams, canals, and other geographical features where water moves from one place to another are also considered bodies of water. Provide the water body type from the pick list. Search for missing terms here: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/envo/classes/http%253A%252F%252Fpurl.obolibrary.org%252Fobo%252FENVO_00000063?lang=en

Definition: A type of area that is populated by humans to different degrees.
Guidance: Provide the populated area type from the pick list.

Definition: An environmental zone which is bounded by material parts of a land mass or the atmosphere or space adjacent to it.
Guidance: Provide the terrestrial environmental zone from the pick list.

Definition: Type of household.
Guidance: Provide the household type from the pick list.

Definition: Link to climate resource information.
Guidance: Provide the link to the climate information, e.g., https://worldclim.org/data/index.html

Definition: The longterm manifestations of WEATHER. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)
Guidance: Provide the climate from the pick list.

Definition: A one-dimensional temporal region which is delimited by the occurrence of processes which serve as its delimiters.
Guidance: Provide the season from the pick list.

Definition: Mean annual temperature.
Guidance: Average temperature over the year. Record the numeric value of the annual mean temperature.

Definition: Mean seasonal temperature.
Guidance: Average temperature over a defined season (e.g., winter, spring, summer, or autumn). Record the numeric value of the mean seasonal temperature.

Definition: Difference between the mean daily maximum and minimum temperatures.

Definition: A genetic characteristics information that is about known changes or the lack thereof from the genetic background, including allele information, duplication, insertion, and deletion.
Guidance:
Select one or more gene alterations associated with resistance from the provided pick list. Gene alterations and their resulting drug resistance classification are sourced from the WHO Compendium of Molecular Markers for Antimalarial Drug Resistance (https://www.who.int/tools/compendium-of-molecular-markers-for-antimalarial-drug-resistance). If a desired alteration is not available in the pick list, select "Other" from the provided pick list and enter the alteration term(s) manually. Multiple alterations are formatted following the conventions in the WHO Compendium:
1 - Multiple alterations within a single gene
Alterations use standard amino-acid substitution notation, separated by a plus sign (+).
Example: crt C72S + K76T + A220S + N326D + I356L
2 - Alterations in multiple genes
Gene symbols are listed, separated by an ampersand (&), followed by their corresponding alterations. 
Example: dhfr & dhps N51I + C59R + S108N & A437G + A581G
3 - Wild‑type codons
Wild-type (reference) codons included in the genotype are grouped in parentheses.
Example: crt (C72C + V73V) + M74I + N75E + K76T
                  crt C72S + (V73V + M74M + N75N) + K76T

Definition: A set of discrete, genetically-linked sequence alterations that reside on the same chromosomal strand and are typically co-inherited within a haplotype block.
Guidance:
Select a haplotype term from the provided pick list. Haplotypes and their resulting drug resistance classification are sourced from the WHO Compendium of Molecular Markers for Antimalarial Drug Resistance (https://www.who.int/tools/compendium-of-molecular-markers-for-antimalarial-drug-resistance). If the desired haplotype is not available, select "Other" from the provided pick list and enter the haplotype manually. Haplotypes are formatted following the conventions in the WHO Compendium: 
gene symbol (codon positions separated by “-”) followed by the amino-acid haplotype representing substitutions at those codon positions. The haplotype letters correspond to the amino acids present at the specified codon positions. 
E.g., dhfr (N51-C59-S108-I164) IRNI; dhps (S436-A437-K540-A581-A613) SGKAA; crt (K76) T; or mdr1 (N86-Y184-D1246) YFD.
